In the first stage, which began on 25 July 2020 and concluded on 29 September 2020, 16 teams were split into two groups in two locations, one in [[Dalian]] and the other in [[Suzhou]].{{cite web|url=http://www.thecfa.cn/zyls1/20200701/28722.html|title=2020中国平安中超联赛将于7月25日开赛|work=Chinese Football Association|date=2020-07-01|access-date=2020-07-01|language=zh}}{{cite news |last1=Stebbings |first1=Peter |title=Cabin fever hits Chinese football's coronavirus 'bubble' |url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/08/21/cabin-fever-hits-chinese-footballs-coronavirus-bubble.html |access-date=21 November 2020 |work=The Jakarta Post |agency=Agence France-Presse |date=21 August 2020 |language=en}} On 2 September 2020, the Chinese Football Association announced that the second stage would begin on 16 October 2020 and conclude on 12 November 2020.{{cite web|url=http://csl-news.9h-sports.com/d_news_MCwxNjk2MA==.html|title=中超联赛总经理会议在苏州举行 第二阶段比赛将于10月16日举行|work=CSL-China.com|date=2 September 2020|access-date=2 September 2020|language=zh}} [[Jiangsu F.C.|Jiangsu Suning]] beat defending champions [[Guangzhou F.C.|Guangzhou Evergrande Taobao]] 2–1 on aggregate [[#Finals|in the finals]] to win their first and only top-flight title: three months after the season, Jiangsu folded. As a result, fourth-placed [[Shanghai Port F.C.|Shanghai SIPG]] gained a place in the [[2021 AFC Champions League]] along with Guangzhou and [[Beijing Guoan F.C.|Beijing Sinobo Guoan]], while [[Cangzhou Mighty Lions F.C.|Shijiazhuang Ever Bright]] avoided relegation. ==Club changes== '''Clubs promoted from [[2019 China League One]]''' * [[Qingdao F.C.|Qingdao Huanghai]] * [[Cangzhou Mighty Lions F.C.|Shijiazhuang Ever Bright]] '''Clubs relegated to [[2020 China League One]]''' * [[Beijing Chengfeng F.C.|Beijing Renhe]] '''Dissolved entries''' * [[Tianjin Tianhai F.C.|Tianjin Tianhai]]{{cite web|url=https://sports.sina.cn/china/2020-05-12/detail-iircuyvi2632246.d.html|title=天津天海官方宣布解散 正式退出中超联赛|work=Sina Sports|date=12 May 2020|access-date=12 May 2020|language=zh}} Shijiazhuang Ever Bright return to the division after a 3-year absence. Qingdao Huanghai compete in the Chinese Super League for the first time in the club's history. Beijing Renhe were relegated to China League One after spending 2 seasons in the Chinese Super League.
